topic: How does interleaved array element spacing affect coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression in Ka-band satellite links?
consensus_response: Interleaved array element spacing affects coverage patterns and grating lobe suppression by influencing beamforming and interference. Tighter spacing suppresses grating lobes, increasing antenna gain and spectral efficiency, but reduces the field of view. Calibration and adaptive compensation methods mitigate issues, while machine learning optimizes beam patterns and interference management.
reference_context: Massive beamforming in Ka-band satellite links requires side lobe suppression technologies to overcome interference and increase spectral efficiency.
